principle: A-001: Separate domain logic from presentation
description: Separation of concerns applied to the user interface: the presentation layer only renders results that the domain computes, so the logic is testable, reusable by other front ends and has one source of truth. Known as Separated Presentation; the antipattern is the Smart UI, where business rules live in screen code.
hierarchy: Separation of concerns (Dijkstra, On the Role of Scientific Thought, 1974)

violations.description: Portfolio analytics live in the Streamlit script: holding period, XIRR per face currency and per bond, the 13% tax on profit only, the minimum holding filter and the ordering. None of it is covered by tests or reachable by other consumers of the library.
The screener ordering by the issuer's best yield is domain logic in the UI.
The screener captions restate the filter thresholds by hand and have already drifted: the ruble caption says 15.5% while the filter uses 15.0%.

description: A check should return a more precise type that carries what it proved, instead of a bool that the caller must remember. Otherwise the knowledge is lost at the type level and code downstream re-asserts it ('shotgun parsing'). Related terms: type-driven design, refinement types.

violations.description: The common screener filters prove that the maturity date and the yield are present but return a bool, so the callers re-establish it with asserts that the type checker cannot verify.

principle: D-003: Don't represent money as binary floating point
description: Monetary amounts are decimal by nature, and binary floating point cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly, so sums, products and comparisons accumulate representation and rounding errors. The established remedy is the Money pattern: an exact type (a decimal or an integer count of minor units) together with its currency and an explicit rounding policy. The antipattern is 'float for currency'; its symptom is epsilon comparisons such as math.isclose in business logic.
hierarchy: Representation error (Goldberg, What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic, 1991)
Money pattern (Fowler, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture, 2002)

violations.description: The ruble amount is a float, and the exact Decimal the SDK provides is converted to float at the boundary, so every downstream amount carries binary representation error.

Money is multiplied by float fractions, quantities and prices and summed as floats, so cash flows, virtual sells, issuer investments and the income total drift by fractions of a kopeck with no defined rounding.
Returned entities and the public API expose money as bare floats, dropping both exactness and the currency.
The repayment quantity is derived by float division and needs an epsilon comparison, and a test pins down tolerance to float error instead of exact arithmetic.

description: A value of the domain type, such as an empty string or zero, must not double as 'no value'. In-band signaling causes the semipredicate problem: the caller cannot tell absence from a legitimate value and the type checker cannot force it to handle absence. The established remedy is an option type (T | None) handled explicitly; related terms are sentinel value and null object misuse.
hierarchy: Null references (Hoare, Null References: The Billion Dollar Mistake, 2009)

violations.description: A missing parent operation is an empty string, so the type cannot tell a missing parent from a real one and the absence check relies on string falsiness.
A bond without an issuer INN is looked up under the key '' and gets a zero investment, so it always passes the issuer investment limit, and all such bonds sort as one issuer.
The yield fallback chain uses `or`, so a real zero yield is treated as a missing one and replaced by the next source.

description: Report an unexpected condition where it arises instead of carrying on with a guess, so the defect surfaces close to its cause rather than as a plausible wrong result far away. Established by Shore, Fail Fast, 2004; the antipatterns it fights are error hiding and silent data loss.
hierarchy: Fail-fast system (Gray, Why Do Computers Stop and What Can Be Done About It?, 1985)

violations.description: A held bond that the screener left out (not buyable now, SPB-only or missing from MOEX) is skipped without notice, so its issuer's investment is understated and the ruble screener can recommend more of an issuer that is already over the limit.

description: Make values immutable unless mutation is their purpose: an immutable object keeps the invariants checked at construction, can be shared freely and never changes behind a caller's back. Related terms: immutable value object, frozen data class, and the 'output argument' smell, where a function changes its argument instead of returning a new value.

violations.description: The workflow fills the missing quantity by mutating the fetched operation in place, an output argument that changes data the caller still holds.

Entities are mutable pydantic models, so their validators hold only at construction: appending to a history's operations can leave it unclosed or mixed with another ticker. Only BondCashFlow is frozen, which makes the entities inconsistent.

principle: D-007: Depend only on public interfaces
description: Use a module only through its published interface; its private names, internals and wire details are free to change. Grounded in information hiding; Hyrum's law describes how depending on unpublished behavior makes every upgrade a breaking change.
hierarchy: Information hiding (Parnas, On the Criteria To Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules, 1972)
Hyrum's law (Winters, Manshreck, Wright, Software Engineering at Google, 2020)

violations.description: The SDK's private _grpc_helpers module, its raw gRPC stub and a hard-coded protobuf field number are used to recover the ticker, so any SDK release may break operations loading silently.
Tests build SDK bonds through the same private helpers.

description: Publish only what consumers need to call the API and read its results; everything else stays private and free to change. Grounded in information hiding and known as 'minimize accessibility'; every extra export becomes a contract that Hyrum's law makes hard to withdraw.
hierarchy: Information hiding (Parnas, On the Criteria To Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules, 1972)
Minimize the accessibility of classes and members (Bloch, Effective Java, 2001)
Minimal interface (Bloch, How to Design a Good API and Why it Matters, 2006)

violations.description: The package exports internal intermediate types and operation type sets that no public function takes or returns and no consumer imports, freezing internals such as AccountBondHistory and the T-Invest operation grouping as public contract.

principle: D-008: Replace primitives with domain types
description: Domain concepts such as a currency code, an ISIN or an INN get their own small types instead of bare strings, so the type checker tells them apart and normalization lives in one place. The antipattern is Primitive Obsession; the remedy is a value object.

violations.description: Currencies are bare strings in two casings ('rub' in the screener, 'RUB' in face units), compared against string literals and upper-cased for display.
Tickers, ISINs and INNs are all plain strings, so the equivalence of a T-Invest ticker and an ISIN is a comment, and the public API returns an untyped dict keyed by INN.
Yields are bare floats in percent while the tax rate and XIRR are fractions, so the unit lives only in comments and display formats, and mixing the two is not caught.

description: A method either changes state (a command) or returns a value (a query), not both, so asking a question never changes the answer. Known as command-query separation; the related architectural pattern is CQRS.

violations.description: FifoPosition.apply both advances the position and returns the fraction to keep, so the fraction cannot be read without moving the position.

description: A literal with domain meaning gets a symbolic constant, so its meaning is stated once and a change happens in one place. The antipattern is the magic number; the refactoring is Replace Magic Number with Symbolic Constant.
hierarchy: Symbolic constants (Kernighan, Plauger, The Elements of Programming Style, 1974)
Replace Magic Number with Symbolic Constant (Fowler, Refactoring, 1999)

violations.description: Rating thresholds and the T-Invest risk level mapping are bare literals, while the neighbouring yield and maturity thresholds are named.
